_about: Editor rules (27 Sep 2026): a promise with no deadline is judged 3 years after it was made; an open-ended promise is marked kept only after 5 years of monitoring (promise_rules.py).

changes.why: No deadline was given, so it is judged 3 years after the 2014 pledge; corruption was not ended.

editorial.summary: Aaj Tak reports that before the 2014 Lok Sabha election Narendra Modi pledged to end corruption with the words 'न मैं खाऊंगा और न खाने दूंगा' (I will neither take nor let others take). The pledge set no deadline; SatyaDheesh judges open-ended promises three years after they are made. In Transparency International's latest Corruption Perceptions Index, India scored 39 out of 100, ranking 91 of 182 countries. Swarajya has reported government action under the slogan, such as the 2019 compulsory retirement of income tax officers; Congress's Jairam Ramesh called it 'a complete hoax' in April 2026.

set.promise: End mafia raj in Uttar Pradesh

changes.why: Monitored for more than 5 years since 2017. Headline trimmed to the commitment he made; 'and crime completely' was the pipeline's wording and no source has him saying it.

editorial.record: Official UP Police figures reported by Deccan Herald put deaths in police encounters since 2017 at 266, with about 11,000 injured, as of December 2025.
editorial.summary: Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister since 2017, has made action against organised crime a signature pledge, telling the Assembly in February 2023 'iss mafia ko mitti me mila denge' (Scroll). In March 2025 he said 'We eliminated these mafias' and that 64,000 acres had been recovered from land mafia (Deccan Herald). Official figures reported in December 2025 put deaths in police encounters since 2017 at 266, with about 11,000 injured. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has alleged 'fake encounters'. NCRB data show UP recorded the most crimes against women in 2023, though its rate was not among the five highest.
editorial.promise_quote: Iss house mein keh raha hoon, [iss mafia ko mitti me mila denge].

editorial.record: Karnataka issued an order for free bus passes for all students after Shivakumar's first Cabinet meeting in June 2026, Deccan Herald reported.
editorial.summary: On 3 June 2026, the day he was sworn in as Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar announced free bus passes for all students on Karnataka's four state transport corporations, extending to boys a benefit girls already had under the Shakti scheme (Deccan Herald). The government issued an order after the first Cabinet meeting; Deccan Herald put the cost at about Rs 1,700 crore a year for over 10 lakh male students. Passes were issued from 12 June, with more than 2,700 issued in the first two days.
